(2) On the render: verify-after/pdp-rope-m-js-full.png, scene section at y 1326 (header 60 + main-product 1266 per verify.json pdp-rope-m-js.sections), the first ~55 px of the photograph show the pill text legibly at top-left; cropped and 2× enlarged it reads «עמידות IP65 / מתאימות לשימוש ח…». Scope: squarely inside the contract — SPEC §1 A line 38 «No scrim, no text on it», SPEC §3 line 139 «rejected if any glyph, badge or icon survives», BRIEF pdp2 §3 rule (4) «No frame with baked text, badges … unless the asset is pre-cropped so the text is outside the file». Evidence holds on the real render for the two claims that matter: verify/dusk-m.png (390) shows line 1 ending «…שמאיר בלילה. יותר» and line 2 «שמש ביום, יותר אור בלילה.» (the shopper's favourite sentence split mid-sentence on the primary viewport), and verify/dusk-d.png + verify-flood/dusk-d.png (1366) show a one-word second line «בלילה.»; sizes.json gives the p as x 692, w 463, h 48, and 463/52 = 8.9 px/ch, i.e. the `max-inline-size:52ch` on line 85 of theme/sections/elmsnest-s-pdp-dusk.liquid is exactly what forces that orphan. Scope: SPEC §1 B does specify one

with both sentences at 52ch, so this is a recorded decision, but the SPEC gives no reason for a single running paragraph (only the facts' hairline rhythm and the ≤160 px cap), SPEC §2 and the file's own header say each sentence keeps its own period, and the `scene` concept the row was borrowed from rendered the two sentences as two separate

Partly confirmed, partly refuted; the finding stands only for lantern 9, and should be re-severed to low with the other two sub-claims dropped.

LANTERN 9 — CONFIRMED (in the file + deployed asset; no real render exists for this product, but object-fit:cover with object-position is deterministic). theme/sections/elmsnest-s-pdp-scene.liquid sets `--ens-op: 40% 50%` for `solar-garden-lantern-9-led`; the asset ens-pdp-lantern9.jpg is 1254×680. At 390×440 the scale is 440/680 = 0.647, the scaled width 811, overflow 421, 40% → band left edge at source x ≈ 261 (at 360: x ≈ 279). In the source frame the solar panel sits at x ≈ 80–210 and the spot head at x ≈ 180–480; my band render (scratch band-lantern9-m-map.png) shows the panel entirely gone and the lens face clipped at the left edge exactly as described. `0% 50%` (band-lantern9-m-fix.png) shows the whole spot with its panel. Two corrections to the designer's text: the product is not «half outside» (the head body is mostly in frame, the panel is what is lost), and at 0% the shrub does NOT «fill the right two-thirds» — it survives only as a sliver on the right edge. SPEC §3 records «40% 50% … confirmed» without a compositional reason, so this is a crop value that fails on the deployed asset, inside the contract.

EDISON at 1366 — observation true, fix wrong, and the cut is inherent to a SPEC decision. Map `--ens-op-lg: 50% 45%` on the 1254² frame → band = source y 333–847 (514 source px tall). Bulb 1's socket is at source y 29–206 and its glass reaches ≈ 640, so the whole bulb is ≈ 640 px tall: NO 560 px band on this frame can hold it whole (the SPEC §1 A block-size 560 at ≥ 901 and §3 «no vertical upscaling» are recorded decisions). The proposed `50% 30%` gives y 222–736: the socket (ends at 206) is STILL outside, and bulb 2 (bright rows 520–843) — the in-focus bulb that the map's 45% keeps whole with its hook and cord — now loses its bottom (band-edison-d-fix.png). The map's crop is the better of the two; this sub-claim is refuted.

STAINLESS at 1366 — refuted on the real render. verify/scene-d.png (the deployed path page) shows the lit stone landing and path between the middle and left lamps across roughly the lower third (band y ≈ 380–560, x ≈ 560–1150) plus the step edge at the lower right; «a picture with no ground in it» is false. The three heads (source y 479–710) are whole with margin. The designer's arithmetic is also off (855−470 = 385 source px ≈ 419 band px, not 530/577), and their own 55% fix disproves «no 560 px crop holds both». `50% 55%` is a legitimate taste alternative, not a defect; the `--ens-h-lg` 640 px proposal contradicts SPEC §1 A without a render failure to justify it.

vote.reason: Evidence is real but the finding is out of scope: it argues against a decision the SPEC records with a reason. Measured on the real render (verify/scene-d.png, verify-wall/scene-d.png, verify-flood/scene-d.png; sizes.json): heading and line boxes do share a top (y 600/600/40, h 48 vs 26) and the glyph rows are heading 602–641 vs line 605–620, so the ~20 px baseline offset exists. But SPEC.md §2 lines 74–75 explicitly fix the ≥ 901 text block as `align-items:start`, gap 48px 64px, "the «one» desktop shot is the reference", and the deployed render reproduces that reference exactly: concepts/one/index.html line 70 uses `align-items:start` and concepts/one/shots/A-d-full.png shows the same relation (heading glyphs y 1234–1270 beside line glyphs 1238–1253, ~17 px offset). The render does not fail the decision; the finding is a taste preference for baseline alignment that the designer judge had in front of them when ranking «one» first. Two further weaknesses: the facts-grid analogy is accurate (.ens-facts__num is a display numeral) but not the SPEC's stated reference, and "zero change to height" is false — with `start` the grid row is max(48, 66) = 66 px; first-baseline alignment pushes the body down ~21 px (row ≈ 87 px, +21), the padding variant +14 px (still inside the ≈200 px desktop text budget of SPEC line 31, current 154 px). Not a defect against the contract; at most a proposal to revise a recorded decision.
